changes.risk_reason: Google is introducing a new opt-in feature that lets services like Search and Gemini pull data from Gmail, Drive, and Photos for personalization and potentially ads, expanding how your private content could be used if you turn it on.
changes.headline: Google will let you opt in to sharing Gmail, Drive, and Photos data across its apps for personalized features and ads.
changes.what_changed: Google added a new option letting services like Search and Gemini access data from other Google services (Gmail, Drive, Google Photos) to personalize your experience, including a new 'Personal Intelligence' feature. Previously excluded content from Drive, Gmail, and Photos can now be used for personalized ads if you choose to allow it.
changes.what_it_means: If you turn this on, information from your private files, emails, or photos could be used by other Google services to tailor search results, suggestions, or ads. By default this sharing is off, but enabling it widens what Google can do with your content.
changes.what_you_can_do: Avoid enabling cross-service personalization features like Personal Intelligence if you don't want data from Gmail, Drive, or Photos used elsewhere. Check your Google Account settings and My Ad Center to review or adjust what data is used for ads.
